title: Fleet work order (dispatch contract)
description: What a dispatch must say: mode, target, truth, authority, scope, finish, report. Generalizes battle-tested operator playbooks into a schema so the delegation contract is enforced, not restated in prose per prompt. Travels with `fleet delegate`; mode presets keep dispatch terse.

title.description: Human-readable title for the target (e.g. from a GitHub issue). Stamped once at dispatch; viewers never fetch.

target.description: Ticket key, PR reference, branch pair, or symptom statement.

truth.description: Authoritative sources, in precedence order — VERIFIED at pickup, never assumed. An explicitly named base outranks older specs. Requirements truth and implementation truth that conflict must surface, not silently resolve.

exclude.description: Checked against the diff at settle; a violation fails the implemented rung.

finish.description: Target rung on the evidence ladder. The runner reports the rung actually reached and may never overstate it.

report.description: Settle payload shape: Status line first (READY/BLOCKED/...), then rung reached vs target, SHAs/PR, verification, self-review, not-done, one exact next action.

continues.description: Post-settle feedback re-entry (#80): this dispatch adopts an existing open PR's head branch instead of creating a fresh job branch. The runner fetches and checks out `branch`, pushes work to it (the PR updates in place), and never opens a new PR. Only valid in followthrough mode — adoption is deliberate; every other mode still trips the claim guard.

branch.description: The PR's head branch, resolved by the CLI at dispatch.

mode.description: assess: binary ready/blocked + blockers, read-only. implement: worktree, smallest complete change, tests, draft PR. investigate: evidence before edits; classify code vs config/seed/permission/deployment; edit unlocks only after the cause is recorded. followthrough: take an existing PR to terminal state. review: read-only quality/PR review. compare: semantic conflict assessment of branches/designs.

authority.description: Capability grants — enforced by the broker (tokens), not requested in prose. v1 hard limits: merge and deploy are never grantable.

merge.description: v1: never grantable. The GitHub token is minted without merge capability.

deploy.description: v1: never grantable. Deploy is out of scope (Post-Build doctrine).

runtime_read.description: Read-only env/log evidence for investigate mode. The only runtime capability in v1.

rung.description: The unified evidence ladder. mergeable is explicitly weak (conflict-free only). merged is a human act (Fleet verifies post-hoc). deployed/runtime-accepted exist on the ladder but are not v1-targetable.

targetableRung.description: Rungs a v1 work order may target. Excludes mergeable (weak, never a goal), merged (human act), deployed and runtime-accepted (out of v1 scope).
